author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Incumbent Lt. Gov. Sabina Matos won Rhode Island’s Democratic primary Wednesday, defeating four challengers as she seeks another term in November.

Matos received about 37% of the vote in unofficial results reported by NBC 10. Former Newport mayor and city councilor Xay Khamsyvoravong finished second, followed by Providence City Council member Sue AnderBois, former state trooper Cindy Coyne and science teacher Ross McCurdy.

Gov. Dan McKee selected Matos for the office in 2021, and voters elected her to a full term in 2022. This year’s result sends her to the general election against Republican John Loughlin. The lieutenant governor’s office has a separate ballot line from the governor in Rhode Island.

Matos said after the primary that she would seek support from voters who backed her opponents and continue work aimed at improving access to fresh food. The result remains unofficial pending the normal canvass and certification process. Her nomination came on the same night McKee lost the Democratic gubernatorial primary, producing a split outcome for the state’s two current executive officeholders.
dek: The incumbent defeated four challengers with about 37% of the unofficial vote and will face Republican John Loughlin in November.
headline: Sabina Matos wins Democratic primary for Rhode Island lieutenant governor
